component.name: Scoria
component.summary: Browse a music library, not a playlist

description.p: Written entirely by AI. No part of Scoria was written by hand: the code, the tests and the documentation were all produced by Claude Code, directed but not line-by-line reviewed by its author. If you are not comfortable running AI-written software, do not install this.

Most players are playlist-centric and treat the library as a source to build playlists from. Scoria inverts that: the library is the primary object, and you navigate it directly. It is aimed at someone with a well-organised local library who listens to whole albums and wants to see a lot of information at once.

ul.li: Cascading filter panes and a dense, sortable, configurable track table, in three layouts that differ only in where the browser sits
Gapless playback: the next track is decoded before the current one drains
ReplayGain read from tags, album gain in album order and track gain when shuffled
Playback is a snapshot, so re-sorting, filtering or searching never disturbs what is playing
Watches the library, so files added or removed are picked up without asking
Media keys, playerctl, and the desktop's own panel, over MPRIS
Full-text search, a queue overlay, album artwork, and a keyboard path to everything

description.p: Scoria never talks to the internet — not for artwork, tags, lookups, updates or telemetry. The library on disk is the only source of truth. That is a decision about what the application is rather than a privacy feature bolted to the side, and the build fails if an HTTP or TLS client appears anywhere in its dependency graph.
The library is assumed to be tagged with MusicBrainz Picard. Supported formats are FLAC, MP3, Ogg Vorbis, AAC and Apple Lossless in MP4, raw AAC, WAV and AIFF.
